scope: Collimated reflector/HUD rendering principles; no new aircraft equipment, historical reticle, optical prescription, ballistic computer or weapon capability.

sources.title: NASA: Head-up display utility II, runway to HUD transitions monitoring eye focus and decision times
sources.use: The primary experiment describes the virtual symbology at optical infinity and explicitly holds its angle subtended at the eye fixed.
sources.implementation: Project a direction from the actual camera, with angular symbol dimensions independent of head translation and viewport resolution. The study does not validate any game's specific historical reticle.

sources.title: NASA-CR-198218: Panoramic, large-screen, 3-D flight display system design
sources.use: The technology survey explains that practical collimated displays have a limited head-motion box. Moving outside it can produce vignetting, loss of resolution or complete image loss.
sources.implementation: Retain actual glass clipping and finite visibility; no screen-wide reticle when the pane or exit pupil is unavailable.

sources.title: US Army Aeromedical Research Laboratory: Helmet-Mounted Displays, chapter 4, page 110
sources.access: Primary-host indexed excerpt consulted; full 54MB PDF was not downloaded because the browser size limit rejected it.
sources.use: Distinguishes true exit-pupil loss from field-of-view loss and reduced quality outside a designed eye box. Eye movement, vibration and slippage affect the usable viewing region.
sources.implementation: Use continuous attenuation and separate lateral/longitudinal eye position. This does not identify an F104 sight or establish its exact eye box.

sources.title: Ansys Optics: Which tools to use when working on a Head-up-Display?
sources.use: Defines the virtual image, eye pupil and eye-box constraints and explains forward evaluation of the image actually seen from different eye positions.
sources.implementation: Separate actual-camera projection from the optical design eye; keep angular symbols aligned with world directions while the physical pane moves in the picture. Automotive example dimensions are not imported into aircraft.

sources.title: BAE Systems: Digital light engine head-up display, 18-C41-02
sources.use: Manufacturer specifications treat luminance, ambient contrast, angular field and positional accuracy as independent display qualities.
sources.implementation: Keep a sharp coloured core with restrained bloom and ambient-dependent display brightness. Modern hardware luminance, angular dimensions, symbols and avionics capabilities are not assigned to F104 or early reflectors.

presentationApproximations.eyeBox: Existing per-model eyeBox extents remain in force. A rounded fourth-power lateral window and smooth axial envelope replace the old max-axis linear ramp; coefficients are game rendering estimates, not measured exit-pupil optics.
presentationApproximations.brightness: Existing renderer sun elevation drives a bounded display contrast curve. The coloured source-over core over additive local bloom is a tone-mapped screen-readability approximation, not absolute photometry or a historical automatic-brightness system.
presentationApproximations.ring: Existing angular ring dimensions and reticle designs are unchanged. Every optical ring now uses the same actual-camera infinity projection as the pipper; the old minimum12pixel computing-ring clamp is removed.

validation: CPU analytical projection and actual drawAirOverlay canvas-command regression only. Browser pixels, cockpit visibility and daylight readability remain pending serial GPU review.

implementation.browserValidation: pending serial review; CPU canvas-command capture does not establish pixels or cockpit readability
